top_comments.text:
As a 40 year old SWE and hiring manager let me throw in some advice:
1. Learning to code takes time. It’s literally a language, don’t expect to speak it in a few weeks. Don’t stress, just do it every day even if it’s just one hour.
2. Every time you learn a new concept. Build something with it. It doesn’t matter how small. It can be a few lines of code. Just put it into action. Think of it like Lego sets. Just make things with it. Play around with things. See how it works.
3. It’s ok to use AI. I do. I use Google every day. Just ask AI to be your tutor: just like a good teacher or tutor, you can ask it to ask you questions to *help* you think rather than replacing your thought; get the juices moving with questions the prompt you to think about things another way. And then ask it to clarify explanations, why certain things are more efficient. If you use AI, genuinely dig deep with understanding things not just accept the answer. Of course that takes alot of time but so what? At the end of it, you’ve accomplished the mission.
